## Problem/question/goal

- Improve Core cognitive classification (e.g., Langa-Weir) using information extracted from HRS/HCAP (possibly measurement and/or prediction models)

- End goal: Cognitive classification, and classification probabilities

## Previous work: the Core algorithm

<div style="font-size: 0.6em; line-height: 1.2;">
The Core algorithm (Analysis A7) exports the HRS/HCAP Algorithm (Manly et al., 2022) to the Core interview with a single domain of general cognitive performance. A factor score from the 8 Core cognitive tests is converted to a demographically adjusted T score, normed in the HCAP robust norms group and rounded to an integer. Two cut points on that score (`r a7_alg$cuts[["severe"]]` and `r a7_alg$cuts[["moderate"]]`) and a self-rated memory rule (D102) define Normal, MCI, and Dementia; respondents with no test score are classified from the Jorm IQCODE (cut points `r sprintf("%.1f", a7_alg$jorm_cuts[["mild"]])` and `r sprintf("%.1f", a7_alg$jorm_cuts[["severe"]])`). The cut points were selected by a rule fixed before any result was seen: match the weighted HRS/HCAP Algorithm dementia and MCI shares, then take the highest weighted dementia kappa.

In HRS/HCAP, survey-weighted agreement of the Core algorithm with the HRS/HCAP Algorithm is $\kappa_w$ = `r f2(kappa_of("Core algorithm", "alg3"))` for Normal, MCI, and Dementia, and $\kappa$ = `r f2(kappa_of("Core algorithm", "alg2"))` for dementia versus no dementia.

The Core algorithm gives each respondent a class. We wanted a probability of each class at the individual level.
</div>
